attempts.summary: Implemented Ansible-based one-way sync of /etc/inventory/app.conf from node1 (source of truth) to node2, orchestrated from node3 (the only node with ansible-core, so it is the control_node). Since node1/node2 (RHEL7) only ship Python 2.7 and ansible-core 2.20 requires Python 3 target modules, the playbook uses ansible.builtin.raw (checksum+base64 read on node1, conditional base64 write on node2) for module-free operation. A root cron job on node3 (*/5 * * * *) runs the playbook, well under the 15-minute requirement; live tests showed propagation in ~90s. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node1, node2, node3) with proven boot_id changes, and post-restart the file, sudo access, cron job, and inventory/playbook all remained intact; a fresh end-to-end change on node1 was auto-synced to node2 after all restarts, confirming full recovery.
